text:
carla: FYI: during today's resilience test we observed a failover race where region B rejected the model artifact we tried to use for warm standby because of a compile ABI mismatch.
yun: can you paste the error?
carla: ```
RuntimeError: ArtifactLoadFailure: abi_version_mismatch
  expected_abi: 2.1.0
  artifact_abi: 1.9.7
  shard: model-embedder-16
Load aborted -> fallback chain triggered
```
ben: That's different from quant differences. This is about compiled kernels / fused op ABI. Means builds vary by toolchain / cuda/cudnn combos.
tess: Why do we have different ABIs across regions? I thought we used hermetic builder images.
carla: We do, but some regions are building with an older toolchain to support older GPU drivers in certain Dedicated clusters. We kept older builders to avoid breaking those pools.
omar: Legal/security note: we have customers in APAC that prohibit moving compiled binaries across countries unless signed with their keys. So copying a build from us-central to apac-south may be blocked. legal-bot: legal: please file a request ticket if you plan cross-border artifact movement for any customer-bound model.
yun: We need a policy + infra: options I see: (A) unify builder images and upgrade older hosts (ops cost), (B) ship multiple compiled artifacts per model ABI and register both with metadata (increases storage + CI matrix), (C) provide an on-host compile shim to recompile artifact from a reproducible intermediate (slower), (D) prevent cross-region failovers for models with ABI mismatch and fall back to smaller in-region model.
ben: Shipping multiple compiled artifacts seems practical. Registry manifest could include `compatible_abis: ["2.1.0","2.0.0"]` and `signing: {}` (signed-manifest_id). Runtime can choose.
tess: But that bumps CI time 3x. And stash storage grows. Also private deployments may force in-region compilation.
omar: For customers with residency clauses, option B only works if their in-region builder reproduces the same artifact and/or signs it.
yun: Could we produce a compact IR (intermediate representation) artifact that is small and portable, then compile to native in-region host during warmup? IR size << weights. That avoids moving weights.
envelope: ops-bot: note: compiling on warm pool will cause increased CPU load and cold-start latency. Recommend pre-compile for standby nodes where possible.
yun: IR compile benchmarks: for medium models IR->native ~ 8s on a 32-CPU warm node, with ~500MB disk IO. Acceptable if pre-warmed or scheduled during quiet windows. Not acceptable for on-the-fly fallback.
ar: carla: Proposal for short term: block automatic cross-region failovers when ABI mismatch is detected (proxy preflight will query artifact manifest). Instead route to a local smaller instance or return degraded response with header `X-Redwood-Degraded: abi_incompatibility`. Increment `region.failover.abi_mismatch.v1` metric.
envelope: ops-bot: implementing policy change: add preflight to proxy to check `artifact.abi` vs `node.accepted_abis`. If mismatch -> consult fallback policy.
ben: Long term: aim for (1) multi-artifact publishing (manifest-based), (2) portable IR + signed manifests that allow in-region native compilation, (3) progressive driver upgrades to reduce CI churn.
tess: Also add manifest metadata fields: `artifact.checksum`, `build_toolchain`, `signed_by`, `restrictions: ["no-cross-border-movement"]`. So proxies and operator UIs can make quick gating decisions.
carla: Agree. Add automation: if artifact has `restrictions` and a cross-region fallback would violate it, fail early and surface clear error to customer + SRE runbook.
omar: Legal wants a checklist for any path that involves cross-border movement or using customer keys. I'll start a stub workflow doc.
yung: (typo) yun: I'll draft a short RFC with: problem statement, short-term block policy, required telemetry (metrics + traces), runbook for operators, and long-term roadmap.
carla: For immediate canary: ops, please pause any active-active failover tests that would exercise this model in apac until we have preflight checks live.
ops-bot: ops-bot: pausing region failover tests for model `embed-2-medium` in apac-south.
legal-bot: legal-bot: raised ticket #L-2026 for cross-border-artifact-policy review.
carla: Thanks all. Please cc ops + legal on the RFC and include an example manifest snippet in RFC. Example manifest snippet idea: ```
{
  "model": "embed-2-medium",
  "artifacts": [
    {"path":"/obj/embed-2-medium/abi-2.1.0.tar","artifact_abi":"2.1.0","checksum":"sha256:...","signed_by":"redwood-build-service"},
    {"path":"/obj/embed-2-medium/ir-v1.tar","type":"ir","checksum":"sha256:...","signed_by":"redwood-build-service"}
  ],
  "restrictions":["no-cross-border-movement"]
}
```
yun: Nice. I'll include feature flags for `preflight-enforce-abi` and `allow-ir-compile` so we can roll safely. ETA RFC: 48 hours.
carla: Solid. End of thread.
